nodes.name: One-step Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The multimetal catalyst as well as the catalyst materials used for control experiments were obtained by a one-step hydrothermal reaction as schematically illustrated in Figure 1a. Hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) serves as C and N source and provides the necessary alkaline environment for metal precipitation, and the morphology of the as-synthesized catalysts was visualized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-resolution scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Binary metal catalyst (CoNi), ternary metal catalyst (CoNiCu and CoNiFe), and quaternary metal catalyst (CoNiFeCu) were all obtained as spherical particles.

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation - all catalysts including CoNiFeCu (1:1:1:0.5) in 1 M KOH on glassy carbon RDE
nodes.source_text: The OER activities of the multimetal catalysts were evaluated using rotating-disk voltammetry on glassy carbon electrodes (0.1256 cm²) in purified 1 M KOH. ... mass loading for all catalysts was ≈0.5 mg cm⁻². For activation, the catalyst-modified electrodes were subjected to 32 cyclic voltammograms (CV) in the potential window from 1.03 to 1.53 V versus RHE at a scan rate of 10 mV s⁻¹. ... CoNiFeCu (1:1:1:0.5) exhibits an overpotential of 291.5 ± 0.5 mV @ 10 mA cm⁻² ... Tafel slopes ... of 43.9 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: OER stability by 2000 CV cycles in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The LSVs of CoNiFeCu (1:1:1:0.5) at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ recorded before and after 2000 CVs are shown in Figure 2c. The two LSVs overlap, indicating the catalyst's excellent stability.

nodes.source_text: The stability was further investigated by chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm⁻² for 25 h in comparison with RuO₂ (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic ratio of metals close to initial precursor molar ratios; Cu decreases from 18.4% to 11.1% after 2h and 6.4% after 20h chronopotentiometry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of the metals in different samples was determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS; inset of Figure S2, Supporting Information). The molar percentage of Cu decreased from initially 18.4% to 11.1%, and further to 6.4% during the chronopotentiometry

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD shows peaks indexed to Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O and Co₂N; broader peaks for CoNiFeCu indicate lower crystallinity/smaller particle size; Cu(OH)₂ peaks for CoNiCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase constitution was investigated by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD)... The XRD patterns contain peaks indexed to a mixture of Ni(OH)₂·0.75H₂O and Co₂N

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice spacings of 0.234 nm and 0.266 nm for Ni(OH)₂ (011) and (100) planes, and 0.217 nm and 0.312 nm for Co₂N (111) and (011) planes in CoNiFeCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM images of CoNiFeCu (1:1:1:0.5) are consistent with the XRD characterization, showing lattice spacings of 0.234 and 0.266 nm, which are ascribed to the (011) and (100) plane of Ni(OH)₂, and interplanar spacings of 0.217 and 0.312 nm, which are consistent with the values for Co₂N(111) and Co₂N(011)

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNiFeCu shows Co 2p3/2 peaks at 780.3, 781.9, 785.7 eV (Co-OH, Co-N, Co2+ satellite); Ni 2p3/2 at 855.3, 861.2 eV (Ni2+-OH); Cu 2p at 932.5, 952.5 eV (Cu+); N 1s at 397.9, 398.9, 400.2 eV (M-N, C-N, N-H); O 1s at 530.5, 531.4, 532.9 eV (OH, O vacancies, adsorbed O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) of the Co 2p core level in CoNiCuFe (1:1:1:0.5) (Figure S6a, Supporting Information), were fitted with three components at binding energies of 780.3, 781.9, and 785.7 eV in the Co2p3/2 spin-orbit. The former two peaks correspond to Co coordinated with OH and N, while the last is a satellite feature from Co2+

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 233, 288, and 541 cm⁻¹ confirm Fe exists as Fe₂O₃ in CoNiFeCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bands at 233, 288, and 541 cm⁻¹ in the Raman spectra of CoNiFeCu (1:1:1:0.5) correspond to pure Fe₂O₃
